To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) the two tests combined (CAS + CM), accounted for 61 % of the variance in the reading comprehension of 42 Grade 6 students; and (b) the two tests correctly classified 91.3 % of the poor readers.

(1) poor reading comprehension is related to poor visual attention and poor magnocellular processing, (2) the combination of poor magnocellular and attention deficits correctly classified 91.3 % of poor readers, (3) poor magnocellular function was a more sensitive predictor of poor reading than attention deficits, and (4) a common linkage between reading comprehension, attention, and magnocular processing exists.

(a) reading disability is associated with deficits in visual attention skills and magnocellular functioning; (b) these deficits are not necessarily the cause of reading disability, but they are concomitants; and (c) the deficits are not necessarily permanent and can be ameliorated by vision therapy and cognitive intervention.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between reading comprehension and magnocellular and attention processing.
the identification and remediation of reading disabilities in children.
the relationship between reading comprehension, attention skills, and magnococular processing.

the visual system is a critical component of the reading system.
the results of this study are consistent with the hypothesis that magnocellular deficits are associated with reading comprehension problems in the absence of visual training.
reading disability is not a single entity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
reading comprehension, visual processing, and visual attention appear to be interrelated, and that the magnocellular system is an essential part of this interrelation.
reading comprehension, visual-attention, and magnocollular deficits are interrelated.
there is a strong relationship between reading comprehension and magnocellular function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the visual system, specifically the magnocellular pathway, plays a critical role in the acquisition and development of reading comprehension.
a common link exists between reading comprehension and visual attention and magnocular processing.
a significant proportion of children with reading difficulties have visual attention and magneto- cellular deficits that can be identified with brief, low-cost, and easy to administer tests.
